scope: Full daily Power Stack research refresh across all tracked categories, every existing idea, US/Hong Kong-China/Malaysia, and every canonical current holding. Research/data only; no site code, UI, scoring, automation or backend changes.
decision: No existing idea earned a formal conviction promotion/demotion today. One genuinely differentiated new opportunity, Aggreko (proposed NYSE: AGKO), clears the research-watch quality/relevance bar but cannot be promoted into the investable universe until IPO pricing/valuation is available.

watch.name: Aggreko
watch.reason: Temporary/behind-the-meter power is a direct time-to-power solution for data centres. Reuters reports H1 2026 revenue +28% to $1.92bn, $80m profit versus a $196m loss, data-centre revenue nearly doubled to $391m for the year ended Jan 3, more than $6bn secured net revenue and >17GW fleet capacity. Differentiated from turbine/grid OEMs because it monetises the waiting period before permanent interconnection.
watch.nextTest: IPO price range, enterprise value, leverage, sponsor sell-down, fleet capex and data-centre customer concentration.

notPromoted.reason: Maverick Power acquisition strengthens data-centre power distribution exposure but NVT is already tracked; deal valuation/integration need monitoring rather than a conviction change.
Grid-connectivity exposure remains attractive, but not differentiated enough versus existing ETN/PWR/GEV/TNB/cable stack at current information set.

macro.read: Physical AI/power demand remains strong while financing quality and valuation discipline remain the key counterweight. Lower oil versus the mid-August spike reduces broad upstream urgency, but refined-product/logistics scarcity remains the more differentiated energy signal. Malaysia power/data-centre momentum remains strong. China strategic technology support remains more compelling than a broad domestic-demand recovery trade.
developingThemes: AI financing quality versus physical power scarcity
very strong El Nino second-order risks
AI ROI/valuation and long-duration financing discipline

categoryReads.Power / Grid: Still highest-quality core category. Fresh confirmation: Southern Cable reports RM1.36bn order book backed by data-centre, renewable and grid-upgrade demand; GE Vernova's power/data-centre order evidence remains exceptional. Aggreko adds a differentiated time-to-power angle. No downgrade to core equipment/grid names.
categoryReads.AI / Data centres: Demand evidence remains strong, but capital intensity means orders/backlog/customer funding matter more than narrative. Prefer power distribution, networking, cooling and advanced packaging with visible orders. nVent's $1.75bn Maverick Power acquisition confirms strategic value of data-centre power distribution but raises integration/price discipline as a watch item.
categoryReads.Nuclear: Hierarchy unchanged: operating generation/components/fuel remain preferred to pre-commercial reactor duration. No fresh evidence justifies upgrading OKLO/SMR relative to CEG/BWXT/1816.HK.
categoryReads.Uranium / Fuel: Cameco Q2 remains on track with annual production outlook unchanged despite spring logistics disruption. Structural contracting/fuel-cycle thesis intact; no conviction change.
categoryReads.Oil & Gas: Maintain integrated majors and gas/LNG infrastructure; keep refiners/product tankers tactical. Do not infer a broad upstream upgrade from geopolitical headlines while crude has eased from recent highs.
categoryReads.Metals: Copper remains preferred structural metal because grid/electrical demand is visible; China/domestic-cycle uncertainty prevents indiscriminate miner beta. Palladium remains lower priority.
categoryReads.Robotics / Automation: Commercialisation order unchanged: warehouse/fixed automation first, cobots/mobile manipulation second, industrial humanoids third, open-world/general-purpose robots last. Symbotic's FY26 Q3 revenue +22% y/y to $721m, $55m net income and $95m adjusted EBITDA reinforce the first-wave warehouse thesis; Aug 25 Stanford Robotics Center affiliation is strategically interesting but not score-changing. Machine vision/components remain preferred picks-and-shovels.
categoryReads.Malaysia: Southern Cable is today's strongest category confirmation, not a new ticker: RM1.36bn order book plus explicit data-centre/grid/NETR demand supports its existing thesis. YTL Power momentum is strong but funding/cash-conversion discipline remains necessary. No genuinely new Malaysian stock clears the existing quality/differentiation bar.
categoryReads.Hong Kong / China: CGN Power's fresh bond issuance and H1 results are consistent with the existing incumbent-nuclear preference; no conviction change without a deeper valuation/earnings delta. ASMPT remains the preferred differentiated advanced-packaging exposure. Broad China tech enthusiasm does not override valuation discipline.

ism.status: Re-verified official ISM pages on Aug 27. July 2026 remains the latest published Manufacturing and Services month; August Manufacturing is scheduled Sep 1 and Services Sep 3.
ism.interpretation: Manufacturing orders/production/backlog and too-low customer inventories still support physical equipment demand; services remains demand-resilient but expensive. Electrical/electronic components, copper, memory, semiconductors, switchgear, transformers and wire/cable remain the Power Stack-relevant bottleneck set. No August data should be inferred from the placeholder page.

existingUniverseReview.summary: Every tracked idea was re-screened against fresh company/category/macro evidence. Relative hierarchy continues to favour generation/grid/electrical/connectivity/reliability, then advanced packaging/cooling/first-wave automation, with greater valuation and financing discipline for contractors, pre-commercial nuclear, humanoids and high-duration AI equities.
